discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 281045
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
545 AM EST Sat Nov 28 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Another round of rain late tonight into Sunday night followed
  by blustery/windy conditions behind a cold front Sunday 
  night. Rainfall amounts between one quarter and three quarters
  of an inch are expected.

- The coldest conditions are expected Monday and Monday night
  followed by a warming trend to much above normal temperatures
  by Thursday and Friday. The next chance of rain will be late 
  in the upcoming work week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 220 AM EST Sat Nov 28 2026

Short wave upper ridging has shifted eastward across the southern 
Great Lakes and Ohio River valley this morning providing a brief 
period of clear skies early this morning. Looking upstream, a lee 
trough feature is progressing eastward and is gaining at least some 
amplitude across the Corn Belt as a 100 knot jet streak shifts 
through the base of this trough. The mid level trough axis 
appears to mark a fairly strong gradient in elevated 900-800 mb 
moisture and this forcing and accompanying moisture axis will 
shift into the local area after 12Z this morning. The limiting 
factor for precipitation continues to be the lack of better near
sfc moisture and maintenance of a relatively dry subcloud 
layer. There have been some reports of light rain upstream 
across eastern Iowa, but in association with cigs of 5-6k feet. 
Did include a mention of chance sprinkles (possibly few 
flurries) following the eastward progression of this forcing 
this morning. By this afternoon, clouds should decrease from 
west to east behind this short wave, with low level warm 
advection becoming a bit more pronounced in its wake. Higher res
guidance does suggest development of modest boundary layer this
afternoon with a few afternoon southwest gusts to 20 mph 
possible.

For tonight, the Mid MS Valley/southern Great Lakes should become 
situated more into a col region as a more vigorous short wave trough 
digs southeast across the Rockies and into the southern Plains.
This will result in a broad sector of strengthening southwest 
flow from the southern plains into eastern Missouri by late 
evening with the nose of this stronger flow beginning to 
impinge on central Indiana toward daybreak Sunday. This 
evolution will allow for rapid northward low level moisture 
transport from the Gulf, and weak speed convergence at nose of 
this stronger low level flow will likely support a wing of 
advective rain overnight into early Sunday morning. These 
leading advective wing precip bands are sometimes difficult to 
pinpoint given they occur well east of the stronger dynamic 
synoptic forcing, so additional refinements in PoPs will be 
needed when confidence in location/timing can be resolved. 

Rain chances should ramp up quickly area-wide during the day Sunday
as digging nature of upper trough and strong moisture transport 
continue, and low/mid level baroclinic zone rapidly strengthens.
This strengthening baroclinicity should also enhance upper jet 
streak magnitude with some additional synoptic contribution in 
left exit region of an Ohio Valley upper jet streak. Given 
PWAT's of close to an inch across NE IN/NW Ohio, storm total 
rainfall amounts in the southeast could reach the half inch to 
three quarters of an inch rain, but progressive nature of best 
moisture axis should prevent any notable hydro issues. Can't 
completely rule out an isolated rumble of thunder far southeast 
with some very weak elevated instability possible, but better 
thunder potential still appears to be across southern Indiana 
for Sunday.

Passage of sfc reflection to the south and the associated 
strong baroclinic zone will mark onset of some stronger 
northwest winds by late Sunday afternoon and more likely by 
Sunday evening/overnight. Strongest isallobaric forcing push may
end up remaining south of local area where RAP suggests 3-hr 
pressure rises on the order of 8-10 mb. This could promote a 
brief period of 40+ mph wind gusts across portions of central 
and possibly into northeast Indiana at least for a brief time 
later Sunday evening. Of greater confidence is wind gusts into 
the 25 to 35 mph range for at least a time Sunday night. Some 
weak lake response is possible late Sunday night in the form of 
a few snow showers, but instability depths in this particular 
setup appear quite shallow.

Winds should drop of noticeably by daybreak Monday as elongated 
north-south oriented low level ridge axis shifts into the region. 
Monday still appears to be coldest day of this period with highs 
likely not getting out of the upper 30s behind this system as low 
level thermal trough anchors across eastern Great Lakes and low
level thermal advection becomes neutral locally.

Confidence remains high in a warming trend for the remainder of the 
week as split-type flow develops across western CONUS with broad 
negative southern stream height anomaly shifting to the southern 
Plains by late Thursday. GFS deterministic remains somewhat of a 
slow outlier in eastward progression of this feature with more 
separation and delayed phasing with northern stream in comparison to 
Canadian/EC. GFS ensemble means do tend to provide a little 
more support to the EC/Canadian camp however. Current trend in 
blended PoPs supports idea of a compromise of these two camps 
with more weight to the non-deterministic GFS consensus in 
higher rain chance PoPs ramping up by late Thursday night. High 
temperatures by Thursday and Friday will be much above normal 
into the 50s and possibly even some lower 60s in some areas by 
Friday depending on precip evolution.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 545 AM EST Sat Nov 28 2026

Midlevel shortwave and associated warm/moist air advection aloft
will pass over the region this morning. Primarily midlevel
clouds expected but some guidance continues to show a brief
period of sufficient top-down saturation to support MVFR
ceilings and perhaps a few sprinkles around 15Z (mainly at
KSBN). Plan to add a TEMPO to address this potential. Clouds
scatter by the afternoon and VFR persists until the next low
pressure system arrives Sunday morning. Best rain chances and
lower ceilings appear to start right at or just after 12Z 
Sunday.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...AGD

spc.text:
SPC AC 280559

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1159 PM CST Fri Nov 27 2026

   Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. today or
   tonight.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At mid-levels, a fast-moving shortwave trough will amplify and move
   southeastward across the central U.S. from today into tonight. Ahead
   of the trough, moisture advection will occur across parts of east
   Texas and the Ark-La-Tex this afternoon and evening. As the trough
   moves into the southern Plains tonight, thunderstorms will be
   possible along and near the moist axis from parts of Arkansas
   eastward into the western Tennessee Valley. No severe threat is
   expected. Elsewhere, thunderstorms are not forecast across the
   continental U.S. today and tonight.

   ..Broyles/Halbert-E.. 11/28/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 280700

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0100 AM CST Sat Nov 28 2026

   Valid 291200Z - 301200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF THE
   SOUTHEAST INTO THE OHIO VALLEY...

   ...SUMMARY...
   At least isolated severe-wind potential may develop across parts of
   the Southeast into the Ohio Valley on Sunday. Some brief-tornado
   threat also cannot be ruled out.

   ...Parts of the Southeast into the Ohio Valley...
   A vigorous mid/upper-level shortwave trough initially over the
   south-central Plains is forecast to move quickly eastward on Sunday,
   eventually reaching the Mid-Atlantic by the end of the period. A
   surface low is forecast to deepen as it moves from the MO/AR border
   region east-northeastward towards the Lower Great Lakes. An
   attendant cold front will sweep through much of the Southeast and
   OH/TN Valleys. 

   A strong (40-55 kt) low-level jet will aid in low-level moisture
   return across parts of MS/AL into the Ohio Valley, though widespread
   cloudiness will tend to limit diurnal heating and destabilization.
   Prefrontal MLCAPE of generally less than 500 J/kg is expected across
   parts of MS/AL/TN/KY, with very weak to negligible instability
   forecast north of the Ohio River. 

   Despite the weak instability, strong forcing will result in
   development of low-topped convection along the cold front. Lightning
   activity may remain relatively limited with this convection, but at
   least isolated severe/damaging gusts will be possible given the
   strength of the flow immediately above the surface. Strong low-level
   shear/SRH could also support brief tornado potential in areas where
   heating/destabilization is relatively maximized.

   The Marginal Risk has been expanded, due to the large area that will
   be affected by low-topped convection within a strong deep-layer wind
   field. Greater wind probabilities may eventually be needed across
   parts of the area, depending on trends regarding prefrontal
   heating/destabilization. The northern extent of the threat is
   uncertain, due to increasingly prohibitive low-level stability north
   of the Ohio River. Along the central Gulf Coast, richer low-level
   moisture will be in place and wind fields will be favorable for
   organized convection, but poor lapse rates and weaker ascent with
   southward extent result in considerable uncertainty regarding severe
   potential in this area. 

   ...Mid-Atlantic into coastal southern New England...
   After an expected weakening trend during the evening, some guidance
   (notably the 00Z RRFS) depicts an increase in low-topped convection
   along the front very late in the period across the Mid-Atlantic into
   southern New England. The current expectation is for low-level
   stability to remain unfavorable for a convective wind threat, but
   trends will continue to be monitored in this area.

   ..Dean.. 11/28/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 280829

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0229 AM CST Sat Nov 28 2026

   Valid 301200Z - 011200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe-thunderstorm potential appears low on Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A powerful mid/upper-level trough initially extending from the
   Carolinas into the Northeast will move quickly offshore early
   Monday. A surface low will move from New England into the Canadian
   Maritimes, as a trailing cold front continues to sweep through the
   Mid-Atlantic and Southeast. The front will slow down and potentially
   stall across the Florida Peninsula, with isolated thunderstorms
   possible along/south of the front within a moist environment. 

   Across the West, a mid/upper-level low and attendant trough are
   forecast to dig southeastward off of the southern California coast. 


   ...Southern New England...
   Strongly forced low-topped convection may be ongoing Monday morning
   across parts of southern New England. This convection may be too
   shallow for lightning production, but some potential for
   convectively enhanced gusts cannot be ruled out in the presence of
   very strong low-level flow. At this time, it appears that lingering
   low-level stability will hamper severe-wind potential in association
   with this convection, but trends will continue to be monitored. 

   ...Coastal Southern California...
   While the approaching mid/upper-level low/trough is expected to
   remain offshore of southern CA, increasing moisture ahead of this
   system may allow for very modest destabilization along coastal areas
   by early Tuesday morning, with showers and isolated thunderstorms
   possible. Wind profiles will become increasingly favorable with
   time, but with the primary low/trough still offshore, initial
   convection may struggle to organize before the end of the period.

   ..Dean.. 11/28/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
